title: The Pharisees accuse Him of blasphemy — Mark 2
paragraphs: The Pharisees accuse Him of blasphemy — Mark 2
And the religious experts called it blasphemy.
That is the shock of Mark 2.

A paralyzed man is lowered through a roof. Everybody expects Jesus to say, “Rise up and walk.” But Jesus goes deeper before He goes public. He says, “Son, your sins are forgiven.” That is when the Pharisees begin burning inside. “Why does this man speak like that? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
They were right about one thing.
But they were blind to the Person standing in front of them.

Jesus did not just heal broken bodies. He came for condemned souls. The greater miracle in Mark 2 is not legs that started moving. It is guilt being lifted by the authority of the Son of God. And when Jesus tells the man to rise, carry his mat, and go home, He proves in the open what He declared in the secret place: He has authority on earth to forgive sins.
Here is where it cuts us.

Religion gets nervous when grace moves with authority. Proud hearts can tolerate a crippled man on a mat more easily than a forgiven sinner walking free. The Pharisees saw a threat. Faith saw a Savior.
And that is still the dividing line today.

Some people want Jesus as teacher. Some want Him as healer. Some admire Him as a moral example. But Mark 2 will not let us stay comfortable. Jesus is either blaspheming—or He is God the Son with power to forgive, restore, and command broken people to stand again.
And that is where grace walks in.

The same Jesus who read the thoughts of the Pharisees saw the faith of desperate friends. The same Jesus who forgave that man still receives the sinner who comes in repentance and faith. Your deepest need is not image repair. Not reputation management. Not behavior polishing. Your deepest need is pardon.
So come honest. Come ruined. Come unable to fix yourself. The One accused of blasphemy is the only One who can speak peace over your sin and power over your paralysis.
He was not stealing God’s glory. He was revealing it.
Repent and believe the Gospel. Christ still forgives. Christ still heals. Christ still calls the dead places in us to rise.
“But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” — Mark 2:10
